doc.title: Bill Goodwin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 28, 2025

chapter: Poconos and the Phil Woods era begins
title: Relocating east and then to the Poconos; Bob Dorough
summary: Moving to New York with a family, then choosing the Poconos in 1970 after visiting Bob Dorough, who became a close friend and mentor.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yes, I think you did. Did you have — did your goals change as things went along? Because you went to the other end of the country to play with Gary Burton, or I’m not sure I’m correct about that but you relocated, is that correct?
Yeah. And then after a few years you went to the Poconos.
Was that a financial decision? An artistic decision?

More of a lifestyle decision. We had lived in California, I grew up there. I lived in my old neighborhood and we had a house. And we got to New York and we didn’t have a house and I was married and had a child, and we, you know we just did sublets or staying with

friends and all of that. But then we got to be, you know I was doing well on the gig and I knew we were going to hang for a while and came out to visit a friend that I had already made in Los Angeles, who I’m sure you knew about, Bob Dorough, the singer- songwriter.

And producer. And Bob and I had worked in L.A. together backing up a folk singer named Chad Mitchell. And so we had become really good friends and also his partner in that was a guitarist named Stuart Scharf, and we all became very, very close friends. And Bob was like an older brother to me. A little like a mentor as much as a guy who just really liked me, we got along great and they started hiring me and all that stuff — when I wasn’t on the road with Gary. And I came to visit him in Pennsylvania in the Poconos — I’m hiccoughing for some reason, excuse me. And we just loved it. So a year after we moved to New York almost exactly to the year January of 1970 we moved out to the Poconos and I basically have had a place out here since then. It’s like 55 years.
